text:
incident-bot: [ALERT] High 5xx rate on frontend-prod (us-east-2) detected at ~1718005400. ELB target-group tg-fe-us2 showing multiple unhealthy targets. EBS I/O errors reported on a subset of EC2 instances. PagerDuty triggered to oncall-sre.

maria (sre): seeing it on grafana too — error budget burning fast. which AZs are hot?

ryan (netops): looks localized to us-east-2 AZ C. ENI rx/tx errors and elevated retransmits. netstack shows kernel drops on several hosts (i-0a1b2c3d...). opening AWS NOC ticket now.

jessica (eng-runtime): logs sample:
```
2024-03-02T17:06:12Z ERROR http 503 upstream request failed: write error: i/o timeout
2024-03-02T17:06:14Z WARN storage ebs: read latency 4200ms, i/o errors
```
curl to /health returns 503 from frontends in azc. backend pods are alive but failing to write to local volumes.

oncall-sre: acknowledged, I'm on the page. quick plan: 1) isolate affected instances from LB, 2) shift weight away from AZ C, 3) enable cross-region traffic spill to us-east-1 for critical routes, 4) open incident bridge. executing now.

maria (sre): +1 on spill. set DNS TTL low (30s) so route53 changes propagate quickly during mitigation. create incident doc in /incidents-runbook.

incident-bot: Created incident INC-20240302-1243 and opened bridge https://calls.example.com/bridge/INC-20240302-1243. PagerDuty: PD-67890.

ryan (netops): AWS update: they confirm degraded network fabric in azc, investigating EC2 host networking. They recommended shifting traffic and will attempt local fabric reroute. ETA 30-90m for root cause / remediation.

jessica (eng-runtime): draining affected nodes and marking targets unhealthy with:
```
aws elbv2 modify-target-group-attributes --target-group-arn arn:aws:...:tg-fe-us2 --attributes Key=deregistration_delay.timeout_seconds,Value=10
aws elbv2 set-target-health --target-group-arn arn:aws:...:tg-fe-us2 --targets Id=i-0a1b2c3d --health-status=unhealthy
```
Also temporarily lowering max connections per instance in our config to avoid overloading remaining healthy hosts.

oncall-sre: changed ALB weights and enabled cross-region failover. command used (internal): `scripts/traffic-shift --from us-east-2 --to us-east-1 --weight 0.9 --critical-only`. Monitoring now.

pm-ops: Support triage note: initial reports from a small subset of dedicated customers in us-east-2 for increased latency and failed requests. drafting customer-facing message to go out if we exceed 30m.

maria (sre): monitoring shows 5xx rate drop after weight shift: 12.4% -> 0.6% within ~6 minutes. EBS errors still visible on i-0a1b2c3d though traffic is routed away so user impact limited.

jessica (eng-runtime): to recover affected hosts we'll replace instances and attach fresh volumes from replicated snapshots where needed. plan: spin new instances in healthy AZs, warm cache, then reattach in maintenance window if required. no customer data loss expected — volumes are replicated and EBS in-use checks show degraded but intact.

ryan (netops): AWS escalated to second-level NOC. They reported a partial fabric forwarding anomaly causing burst drops for ENIs in AZ C. Their temporary mitigation involved hypervisor-level reroutes. Continuing to watch.

incident-bot: AWS ticket updated: 1234567890. Notification sent to infra@redwood.com.

oncall-sre: starting runway to handoff to night oncall at 18:00 UTC. leaving notes on bridge: traffic shifted, 5xx back to baseline, AWS working on AZ fabric, replacing affected hosts as follow-up.

maria (sre): documenting impact window: 17:05-17:48 UTC (partial degradation). Estimated 10-12% of requests in azc experienced errors before mitigation; after shift ~95% of traffic served normally. owner for postmortem: jessica.

pm-ops: support blurb ready: "We detected a regional networking issue in us-east-2 that caused intermittent errors for a small subset of customers. We mitigated by shifting traffic and working with AWS; no data loss is expected. Updates to follow." ready to send on approval.

oncall-sre: handoff complete. leaving monitoring alerts at reduced sensitivity. will re-escalate if AWS indicates regression. :wave:

incident-bot: Incident INC-20240302-1243 status -> mitigated (monitoring). Next step: postmortem and timeline in 24 hrs.

maria (sre): add note to postmortem: consider adding automatic cross-region spill triggers for ELB target-group health thresholds, and a runbook section for EBS degraded IO.

jessica (eng-runtime): copying logs and timestamps to incident doc. will own postmortem and customer impact section.

ryan (netops): AWS final note: fabric-level fix deployed to AZ C, monitoring for residual ENI errors. marking AWS NOC ticket resolved but will keep an eye for recurrences.

oncall-sre: closing active bridge. follow-ups in #incidents and the postmortem doc. :white_check_mark:
